newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran blasts U.S. over U.N. resolution.
newsitem.headline: Iran blasts U.S. over U.N. resolution.

text.p: Iranian leaders returned to the offensive against the United States for its veto of a United Nations resolution condemning Israel's decision to build Jewish homes in East Jerusalem.

In separate speeches on Sunday the Islamic republic's supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and parliament speaker Ali Akbar Nateq-Nouri blasted the United States for Friday's veto of a draft resolution backed by all 14 other members of the Security Council.
Khamenei told an audience in the southwestern city of Abadan that Israel destroyed people's houses in Jerusalem and made them homeless.

"The world, at least, raises a cry in response to this tragedy. It raises some protests. However, as soon as they want to approve a resolution in the Security Council against this blatantly unjust act -- and no fair person could describe the magnitude of this injustice -- the regime of the United States of America vetoes the resolution," he said.
Tehran radio, monitored by the British Broadcasting Corporation, relayed the speech and also broadcast the crowd's repeated response: "Death to America".
In another speech to worshippers at a mosque in the western city of Khorramshahr, Khamenei said that things in Iran would not possibly change to suit the preference of the United States.

He said the U.N. resolution was one of the very few fair resolutions debated by the Security Council. "However, the tyrannical USA, this ignorant bully, vetoed it. This is the true face of international politics."

In Tehran, Nateq-Nouri told an open session of parliament that Israel's policy indicated the anti-human, anti-Islamic and domineering nature of the Zionist regime, the official news agency IRNA reported on Monday.
He said the conspiracy had been designed in cooperation with the United States to separate the Arab eastern part of Jerusalem from its other Moslem-populated parts.

Nateq-Nouri, who appears to be in the lead in campaigning for Iran's presidential election in May, condemned the U.S. veto and said Washington had planned to turn Israel into the gendarme of the region and help it dominate the world of Islam.

"Moslem nations should know that as revealed by Iran from the beginning the so-called Middle East peace process is nothing but a plot and treason against the Palestinians and an opportunity for the Zionist regime to launch more aggressions," he added.
